primary_action.input: Tab to the selected radio, ArrowDown to Proof B, Tab and Enter.
primary_action.expected: Reject B because its right end is misregistered.
primary_action.observed: The button changed to Release proof B; the verdict said to hold B because the left crosses meet but the right copper cross tilts away.

A-1440.edge_observation: ArrowDown selected C; releasing it produced 'Ready to print. Both copper crosses align with teal.' Captures: A-1440-before, A-1440-after, A-1440-edge.
A-1440.fact_check: Before interaction, I predicted C: its left and right marks each looked like a single cross. A had visibly offset crosses at both ends; B appeared aligned on the left and tilted on the right. Both ends were in the opening viewport. A was initially selected and its release button was available despite the visible mismatch, which could suggest readiness.
A-1440.strength: The ticket strip puts all three alternatives and both ends side by side, making comparison immediate. Its perforated silhouette fits the box-office subject.
A-1440.weakness: The thin overlapping marks are small, and the ticket's type and rectangular strip are less memorable as artwork than the registration exercise itself.
A-1440.repair: Enlarge the marks or add a compact magnified comparison, and label the action as a check so the initial selection does not imply approval.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected radio, ArrowDown to Proof B, Tab and Enter.
primary_action.expected: Reject B because its right end is misregistered.
primary_action.observed: The verdict said to hold B and identified the tilted right copper cross.

A-390.edge_observation: Selecting C with the keyboard and activating its button produced the ready-to-print verdict. Captures: A-390-before, A-390-after, A-390-edge.
A-390.fact_check: Before interaction, I predicted C: its left and right ends looked like single overlapping crosses. B's left cross looked aligned while the right was visibly tilted; A's two ends were offset. Both ends and all three proofs were in the opening viewport. The preselected A and 'Release proof A' could misleadingly suggest it is ready.
A-390.strength: The whole ticket comparison and primary action fit in the opening viewport, with a clear focus outline during keyboard use.
A-390.weakness: The marks remain fine and the copper and teal overlap is difficult to distinguish at phone size; the ticket silhouette is recognizable but visually simple.
A-390.repair: Provide larger registration details and change 'Release' to 'Check' until a verdict is known.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B, Enter, then Tab to Check this proof and Enter.
primary_action.expected: Reject B because only its left end aligns.
primary_action.observed: The left detail said both inks align, the right said red is below blue, and the verdict described the rotated proof.

B-1440.edge_observation: Selecting C showed alignment at both ends; checking it returned 'Ready to print. Both red diamonds sit on the blue crosses.' Captures: B-1440-before, B-1440-after, B-1440-edge.
B-1440.fact_check: Before interaction, the ready proof was unclear because only A's marks were shown. At both visible ends, A's red diamond sat to the right of the blue cross. Both ends were in the opening viewport. A was selected, but its offset marks and explanatory text did not depict it as ready.
B-1440.strength: The wave field, crossing red bands and central disc give the poster a memorable silhouette; enlarged, labeled end marks connect the art to the registration task.
B-1440.weakness: Only one proof can be inspected at a time, so identifying the ready one requires cycling through choices. The small marks on the poster itself are harder to read than the separate details.
B-1440.repair: Offer a compact comparison of all three proofs while retaining the enlarged end details and poster.

primary_action.input: Tab to Proof B and Enter; navigate to Check this proof and Enter.
primary_action.expected: Reject B because its right end is misregistered.
primary_action.observed: The left detail said both inks align, the right said red is below blue, and the verdict described the rotated proof.

B-390.edge_observation: Selecting C and checking it returned the ready-to-print verdict, with both details labeled aligned. Captures: B-390-before, B-390-after, B-390-edge.
B-390.fact_check: Before interaction, the ready proof was unclear because only A was displayed. Its left and right red diamonds visibly sat to the right of their blue crosses. Both ends, the proof controls and the action were in the opening viewport. The selected A did not look ready in the enlarged details.
B-390.strength: The poster's crossing bands remain distinctive on mobile, and the paired detail panels explain the mismatch in both graphic and text.
B-390.weakness: The poster's own registration marks are tiny, and the alternatives cannot be compared without selecting them. The layout width reported by the review tool was 375 CSS pixels in the 390-pixel view.
B-390.repair: Keep the enlarged end details prominent and add a compact way to compare proof states without relying on the tiny poster marks.

preference.reason: B combines a more memorable print silhouette with larger, labeled registration details and specific rejection and recovery feedback. A makes comparison faster, but its small cross marks and initially available 'Release proof A' action weaken the proof-reading task.

A-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab, ArrowDown, Tab and Enter selected and checked Proof C. The status said it was ready to print. Captures: A-1440-before, A-1440-after, A-1440-edge.
A-1440.fact_check: Before interaction, I predicted C: at both ends a copper diamond surrounds a teal cross, with the cross appearing near the diamond's center. The shapes remain visibly distinct. Both ends are in the opening viewport. B's left end also looks aligned, but its right diamond is visibly low and tilted. The later verdict confirmed C; exact mechanical alignment cannot be established from the screenshot alone.
A-1440.strength: The ticket silhouette, perforations and oversized condensed title make the exhibit memorable. The distinct cross and diamond make the comparison intelligible.
A-1440.weakness: The small registration marks require close inspection, and the initially selected A could imply an endorsed choice.
A-1440.repair: Enlarge the marks or offer a close inspection view, and consider starting without a selected proof.

A-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab, ArrowDown, Tab and Enter selected and checked C, yielding the ready-to-print verdict. Captures: A-390-before, A-390-after, A-390-edge.
A-390.fact_check: Before interaction, I predicted C: the teal cross sits approximately within a separate copper diamond at both the left and right ends. Both ends are visible in the opening viewport. B's left end resembles C, but its right diamond visibly drops and tilts. The later verdict confirmed C; pixel-level alignment is not independently established.
A-390.strength: The complete ticket, both ends and action fit in the opening viewport; its pink perforated shape and large title retain a distinctive silhouette.
A-390.weakness: The marks are small on a phone, and preselected A has the same lighter row treatment later used to indicate a chosen proof.
A-390.repair: Make the marks larger while preserving both ends on screen, and distinguish selection from readiness more explicitly.

B-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab, ArrowDown, Tab and Enter selected and checked C. The status said both copper crosses align with teal and C was ready to print. Captures: B-1440-before, B-1440-after, B-1440-edge.
B-1440.fact_check: Before interaction, I predicted C: both ends look like single dark horizontal-and-vertical crosses. The copper and teal strokes merge visually, so their individual positions cannot be distinguished there from the rendered image. Both ends are visible initially. B's left end also looks like a single cross, while its right has visibly tilted copper strokes. The verdict confirms the intended C result, but the screenshot alone does not prove both inks are present at its aligned ends.
B-1440.strength: The perforated pink ticket and bold Night Machine title give the page a memorable silhouette; the incorrect tilted mark is easy to spot.
B-1440.weakness: The aligned inks merge into a dark cross, making the two-ink registration concept less self-evident. A is selected initially despite being wrong.
B-1440.repair: Use distinguishable registration shapes or another visible cue that preserves both ink identities when aligned.

B-390.fact_check: Before interaction, I predicted C: the left and right ends each appear as one dark cross with horizontal and vertical strokes. The two ink positions merge visually, so I cannot separately see copper and teal on the aligned marks. Both ends are in the opening viewport.
